newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta to appoint Bre-X prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: Alberta to appoint Bre-X prosecutor.

text.p: The Canadian province of Alberta on Tuesday appointed a special prosecutor to look into the scandal surrounding Bre-X Minerals Ltd, the Canadian Press news agency reported.

An independent audit released on Sunday concluded that Bre-X's Busang gold discovery in Indonesia -- once touted as one of the biggest this century -- contained no gold worth mining and said data had been falsified on a massive scale.

Alberta Premier Ralph Klein said on Tuesday the matter would be fully investigated before a decision was made whether to lay charges. The province's special prosecutor will work with the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP).

"It will be investigated to its fullest extent and if there's evidence of criminal activity, those responsible will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law," Klein said according to Canadian Press.

Alberta Justice Minister Jon Havelock said the province would not take a lead role in the investigation. "It's up to the RCMP to determine how they wish to conduct their review," he told Canadian Press.
"They are the primary people responsible for that and we will be advising with respect to whatever they bring back."
The minister would not discuss logistics of the investigation, including whether the special prosecutor might travel to Indonesia.
The news agency said an Alberta government pension fund had invested in Bre-X stock which collapsed after Sunday's news. Klein played down the investment, saying it was "a very, very small amount."
